notes: §1985:IX.4.4.4 GR12: "When the EXTEND phrase is specified and the LABEL RECORDS clause indicates label records are present, the execution of the OPEN statement includes the following steps", of which a to c process the beginning and ending labels as for INPUT and d is "Processing then proceeds as though the file had been opened with the OUTPUT phrase". The label steps are the implementor's (§1985:C.2 item 61: "The labels are checked or written in accordance with the implementor's specified conventions for input or output label handling"). The implementation's convention is that a file carries no label the COBOL program can see: labels belong to the host file system (the standard's own ground for making the clause obsolete, §1985:C.1: "Specifying the presence of file labels is considered a function of the operating system and as such does not belong in the COBOL program"), and docs/VERSION_CHANGE_REFERENCE.md Table 7 row 7.4 states it as 'accepted-inert at 85'. The clause is parsed at 85 (FileDescriptionFormats.Rows admits it in every FD format; VersionConformancePass.VisitLabelRecordsClause refuses it from 2002, COBOL0902) and no binder or runtime member reads it, so KeyedConnector.OpenCore opens a file the same way under LABEL RECORDS ARE STANDARD, LABEL RECORD IS OMITTED and no clause. With no label to process, steps a to c have no action, and step d is the EXTEND arm of OpenCore followed by IndexedConnector.Opened, which positions after the highest prime key (§1985:IX.4.4.4 GR11) so that the WRITE statements that follow add records as an output file's do. Probed at --std 85: OPEN EXTEND under STANDARD and under OMITTED both answer 00, keep the existing records, accept a higher key and refuse a lower one with status 21. The witness extends a LABEL RECORDS ARE STANDARD indexed file and reads both records back. Not covered by this verdict: the clause's own syntax is unchecked at 85 (kb/Work PB5070), and docs/CONFORMANCE.md has no entry for the 1985 implementor-defined list's label items (§1985:C.2 items 60 and 61), so the convention is written down only in the VCR row.

next.reason: 1985: "When the EXTEND phrase is specified and the LABEL RECORDS clause indicates label records are present, ... These labels are then deleted."; 2023: "GR-14.9.27.4-15 only positions the file after the last logical record; no LABEL RECORDS clause or label processing is stated.". 2023 OPEN EXTEND rules cover positioning but say nothing of label records. The LABEL RECORDS clause and its label processing are absent from the 2023 candidates.
